title: An infeasible subsystem as lines a planner can read

blocks.text: A transport planner's model is infeasible, and the team has a `mathopt.ComputeInfeasibleSubsystemResult` for it, from Gurobi through `compute_infeasible_subsystem` or from a hand-made deletion filter (lesson 4.3.5). Write `explain(result)`, which turns it into sorted lines the planner can read:

rows: a row in `linear_constraints` with its `lower` side
a variable in `variable_bounds` with its `lower` side

blocks.text: Bounds are written with `:g` (so 120.0 prints as `120`). List only the sides the subsystem marks: an equality row can be in it with only one side. If `result.feasibility` is not `INFEASIBLE`, the subsystem means nothing and the function returns an empty list. Return the lines sorted. About twelve lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

from explain import explain

B = mathopt.ModelSubsetBounds

# A barge plan: tonnes must reach 90, the quay takes at most 70.
model = mathopt.Model(name="barge")
tonnes = model.add_integer_variable(lb=0, ub=80, name="tonnes")
quay = model.add_linear_constraint(tonnes <= 70, name="quay")
order = model.add_linear_constraint(tonnes >= 90, name="order")
subset = mathopt.ModelSubset(linear_constraints={order: B(lower=True), quay: B(upper=True)},
                             variable_bounds={tonnes: B(upper=True)},
                             variable_integrality=frozenset({tonnes}))

for status in (mathopt.FeasibilityStatus.INFEASIBLE, mathopt.FeasibilityStatus.FEASIBLE):
    found = mathopt.ComputeInfeasibleSubsystemResult(feasibility=status, infeasible_subsystem=subset, is_minimal=False)
    print(f"lines when {status.name}:", explain(found))

cases.says: two rows whose upper sides clash are listed as two lines, sorted
a FEASIBLE result gives no lines while an INFEASIBLE one with the same subset gives lines
an equality row of which only the lower side is in the subsystem gives only its lower line
a variable's bound and another's integrality in the subsystem each give a line
